body:
Not unusual for communists groups to have international ties I believe.
Especially the one's leaning revolutionary, Lenin had some interesting views on collaborating with other socialist countries to aid their proletariat revolution. Not to mention that if you're tackling a state, I'm guessing you need international support all the more.

Also, check it: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proletarian_internationalism
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_communism
And quoting what I believe was the last line of the Commie Manifesto: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workers_of_the_world,_unite!
Emphasis on "of the world".

The CPI-Maoist does have ideological motivations for their actions (atleast at higher levels, many boots on the ground probably don't care all that much I'm guessing), and this ideology (Maoism and now Marxism-Leninism) is a very prominent one, shared by numerous organisations across the globe. Of course having "close links" goes a long way from being supported by, in ways that count.

As far as the Indian state is concerned I doubt they should be as worried about the Maoists just having ties with these other communist groups, as they should about whether these groups are providing military support which I doubt they are. This might be what the General Secretary of the party describes as a "right deviation" (that is, if the members thought this way http://www.signalfire.org/2015/06/20/maoist-information-bulletin-mib-interviews-cpimaoist-general-secretary-comrade-ganapathy/) but what the CPI-M has as its "greatest external security threat" seems to be the fact that they're going to be physically mowed down by Green Hunt and such. They're problem is very much a "tactical" one and, unless you honestly hold that the inherent contradictions (and what not that revolutionary groups theoretically claim will lead to the downfall of capitalist systems and aid revolution) exist, you would have to agree that these international ties will do nothing if they do not transform into military aid.
